mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be positive due to lower real borrowing costs and increased equity discounting.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In the trigger regime, 20-day forward returns are not statistically outperforming the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coincident with rising consumer confidence (HOUST) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as labor market expansion supports corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 3 months AND HOUST > previous 3 months by at least 10% in the same month
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the 20-day return during the preceding 60 days (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend for two consecutive months predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market anticipates stronger economic momentum.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative or indistinguishable from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified demand expansion period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to weakening supply-side conditions and reduced corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < moving_avg(INDPRO, 12 months) for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the supply contraction (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% for three consecutive months coincides with a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), signaling a risk-off environment that depresses equity valuations and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.5 for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < previous 3 months
failure_condition: During the trigger period, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual: a sharp rise in PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in RSAFS for two months indicates labor market imbalances that precede a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous 3 months AND RSAFS < previous 3 months by at least 15%
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 20-day forward return is not statistically worse than the 20-day return during the prior 60 days (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains below trend for four consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 5-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent supply-side weakness and reduced corporate investment plans.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive or not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) during the identified contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time surprise cut in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25 percentage points at the policy meeting date predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate lower future borrowing costs and improved liquidity.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by > 0.25pp in a single month relative to previous month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (p > 0.05) during the post-cut period.
